commands.name: ingest
commands.help:
Ingest pipeline results into a Depictio server, from validation to dashboards.
Formerly `run`.

Runs these steps in order:
  1. Check that the server answers
  2. Check the S3 storage configuration
  3. Validate the project configuration (or resolve the template)
  4. Sync the project configuration to the server
  5. Scan the data files
  6. Process the data collections, uploading images where local_images_path is set
  7. Run the table joins the project configuration defines
  8. Import the dashboards the project lacks (from the template, or from --dashboard)

Example, the template detected from the results directory:
  depictio ingest results/

Refreshed after a new run, the dashboards kept as edited in the viewer:
  depictio ingest results/ --update-config

A manifest-driven template, the files listed in a manifest instead of a directory:
  depictio ingest --template generic/manifest-tables/1 --manifest https://data.example.org/run42/manifest.json
commands.short_help: Ingest pipeline results into a Depictio server, from validation to dashboards. Formerly `run`.

params.name: data_dir
params.help: Directory of the pipeline results to ingest, or an s3:// prefix holding them (e.g. s3://my-bucket/pipeline/run42). Without --template or --project-config-path, the template is detected from it. Formerly `--data-root`.

params.name: server
params.help: Server to use: 'local' for the one `depictio local up` runs, or a CLI configuration file. Default: $DEPICTIO_CLI_CONFIG_PATH, else ~/.depictio/CLI.yaml, else the local server. Formerly `--CLI-config-path`.

params.name: template
params.help: Template to build the project from, e.g. nf-core/ampliseq/2.16.0, or nf-core/ampliseq/latest for the newest shipped version. Default: detected from DATA_DIR, else composed from the catalog. Not with --project-config-path.

params.name: manifest
params.help: A data manifest, as an https:// URL or a local file, listing the files to ingest as {id, type, url[, run]} entries. In place of DATA_DIR, for a manifest-driven template such as generic/manifest-tables/1 (it sets the template's MANIFEST_URL variable).

params.name: project_config_path
params.help: Project YAML, for a pipeline Depictio ships no template for. Not with --template.

params.name: update_config
params.help: Refresh a project that exists: its configuration, and its tables with every run rescanned. Its runs become those of DATA_DIR (or of the project file's locations) and those added with --attach-run; the runs of any other location are removed. Its dashboards are kept as they are, edits made in the viewer included; the template's dashboards it lacks are added. A project not on the server yet is created.

params.name: var
params.help: Extra template variable as KEY=VALUE. Repeatable. Example: --var SAMPLESHEET_FILE=/path/to/samplesheet.csv --var METADATA_FILE=/path/to/metadata.tsv

params.name: dry_run
params.help: Validate the project configuration locally and list the steps that would run, without contacting the server

params.name: project
params.help: Project name. Replaces the name the template gives, or the `name` in the --project-config-path file. --attach-run and --update-config find the project by it. Formerly `--project-name`.

params.name: attach_run
params.help: Add DATA_DIR to an EXISTING project as one more run, instead of creating a project. The run is recorded as attached, so a later --update-config keeps it. The project is found by --project, else by the template's own name. Implies --update-config, dashboards included. Only the new run's rows are written; a recipe that mixes samples (distances, ordinations, top-N) is recomputed over every run, see --per-run.

params.name: drop_missing_runs
params.help: On a refresh, remove the runs of a location added with --attach-run that is not on this host. Without it, such a refresh stops before changing anything.

params.name: provenance_file
params.help: Extra provenance/recap file (json, yaml, or 2-column tsv of key/value) whose entries are listed in the project's run-provenance report under 'User provided'. Repeatable.

params.name: bind
params.help: Point one data collection at where its data actually is, as TAG=LOCATION. Repeatable. The scan mode is inferred from the location: a local directory or glob scans locally, a local file is a single file, https:// is a remote file, an s3:// prefix or glob is listed remotely. Example: --bind samples=s3://my-bucket/run42/*.samples.csv

params.name: dashboard
params.help: Dashboard YAML file to import instead of the template's own. Repeatable.

params.name: dashboard_name
params.help: Title of the main dashboard. Without it, a new dashboard takes the title in its YAML and a refresh keeps the current one, even if renamed in the viewer. With it, a refresh renames the existing main dashboard and leaves its contents as they are. Child tabs keep their titles and stay attached.

params.name: reset_dashboards
params.help: Import the template's dashboards (or --dashboard's) over the ones the project has: the layout and components edited in the viewer are lost, the titles are kept. Implies --update-config, as only a project that exists has dashboards to reset.

params.name: workflow_name
params.help: Scan and process only this workflow (its tag)

params.name: data_collection_tag
params.help: Scan and process only this data collection

params.name: skip
params.help: Steps to skip, comma-separated or repeated: server-check, s3-check, sync, scan, process, join, dashboards. Skipping process skips the image upload too. Formerly the `--skip-<step>` flags.

params.name: continue_on_error
params.help: Continue execution even if a step fails

params.name: compose
params.help: Compose the template from what the catalog recognises in DATA_DIR, even when a bundled template fits. Without it, composing is the fallback when none does.

params.name: include_unknown
params.help: When composing: also ingest the tabular files the catalog does not recognise, in an 'Other data' tab.

params.name: include
params.help: When composing: ingest the unrecognised files matching this glob, relative to DATA_DIR (e.g. 'stats/*.tsv'). Repeatable.

params.name: pipeline_id
params.help: The pipeline that produced the data, as '<name>/<version>' (e.g. 'nf-core/ampliseq/2.16.0'). Without --template or --project-config-path, the bundled template that matches it is used; otherwise it is ignored. Pipeline triggers fill it in, from a Nextflow pipeline's workflow.manifest for instance.

params.name: triggered_by
params.help: What invoked this ingestion, recorded on the project and shown in its ingestion report. Defaults to 'manual'; a pipeline's completion trigger passes its engine (e.g. 'nextflow') so an automated project is distinguishable from one someone ingested by hand.

params.name: user
params.help: Provision (create-or-get) this user's account and run the pipeline as them, then emit a passwordless login link to their dashboard. Requires --provisioning-key.

params.name: provisioning_key
params.help: Shared provisioning secret used with --user (or set DEPICTIO_AUTH_PROVISIONING_API_KEY).

params.name: result_json
params.help: Write how the ingestion ended (status, project and dashboard ids and links) to this file as JSON, for scripts.

params.name: sync_changed
params.help: Re-upload only the files whose size or modification time moved since the last scan. Narrower than --update-config, which re-uploads every file.

params.name: write_mode
params.help: How step 6 writes a table. overwrite: rewrite it whole. replace-runs: partition it by run and rewrite only the runs in this batch, leaving the others untouched.

params.name: incremental_write
params.help: With --write-mode replace-runs, rewrite only the runs that changed instead of rebuilding the whole table. Falls back to a full rebuild whenever that cannot be done safely (run removed, table not partitioned by run, column type changed).

params.name: per_run
params.help: Compute every recipe once per run, including those that mix samples (distances, ordinations, top-N cuts), which are otherwise recomputed over all the project's runs at once. Their per-run outputs are then stacked.

params.name: skip_unchanged
params.help: Leave a data collection's table untouched when the scan found no new, changed or removed file for it. Off by default, so that ingesting again always rebuilds a project that drifted.

params.name: repartition
params.help: Let --write-mode replace-runs partition by run a table that is not yet. This rewrites every row, so it is never done implicitly, and never by the watcher.

params.name: streaming
params.help: Stream the Delta write instead of materialising the whole table in memory (lower peak RSS on large ingests). Experimental; falls back to the standard write on any failure.

params.name: concurrency
params.help: Parallel HTTP requests for file uploads and cleanup deletes

params.name: upload_chunk_size
params.help: Files per /files/upsert_batch request

params.name: state_cache
params.help: Skip the runs whose file tree is unchanged since the last successful scan, from a local cache. Only applies when rescanning.

params.name: async_upsert
params.help: Ask the server to profile each written table in the background, and poll until it finishes, instead of holding one long request open. A server without offloading enabled ignores it and answers inline.

params.name: preview_recipes
params.help: Show recipe input sources and transformed output before writing to Delta Lake

params.name: rich_tables
params.help: Show detailed summary of the workflow execution

commands.name: watch
commands.help:
Ingest pipeline results, then again whenever they change: `ingest` on a loop.

The first cycle runs at once and refreshes the project as `ingest
--update-config` does; the later ones rescan and rewrite what moved. Runs until
interrupted: SIGINT or SIGTERM finish the cycle in progress and then exit
cleanly, so it is safe to run under systemd or as a container command.

One watcher or ingestion per project at a time: the first cycle takes the
project's lock before it writes anything, and the watch holds it until it
exits. A second one stops at once and names the lock file.

Example, rewriting only the runs that changed:
  depictio watch results/ --write-mode replace-runs --incremental-write
commands.short_help: Ingest pipeline results, then again whenever they change: `ingest` on a loop.

params.name: data_dir
params.help: Directory of the pipeline results to watch. Without --template or --project-config-path, the template is detected from it, as `ingest` does.

params.name: server
params.help: Server to use: 'local' for the one `depictio local up` runs, or a CLI configuration file. Default: $DEPICTIO_CLI_CONFIG_PATH, else ~/.depictio/CLI.yaml, else the local server. Formerly `--CLI-config-path`.

params.name: template
params.help: Template to build the project from, as for `ingest`. Default: detected from DATA_DIR. Not with --project-config-path.

params.name: project_config_path
params.help: Project YAML, for a pipeline Depictio ships no template for. Not with --template.

params.name: project
params.help: Project name. Replaces the name the template gives, or the `name` in the --project-config-path file.

params.name: var
params.help: Extra template variable as KEY=VALUE. Repeatable.

params.name: mode
params.help: incremental: re-upload only the files that changed. full: re-upload and rewrite everything on every cycle.

params.name: backend
params.help: auto (detect), native (filesystem events only), polling (periodic re-walk), or both. auto selects polling on network filesystems, where native events do not see writes made from another host.

params.name: debounce
params.help: Seconds of quiet before a cycle is triggered

params.name: settle
params.help: Seconds a file must hold the same size and mtime before it is ingested

params.name: interval
params.help: Seconds between polling walks (also the backstop for lost events)

params.name: max_delay
params.help: Ceiling on debouncing, so a tree written continuously still gets ingested

params.name: full_every
params.help: Run a full cycle every N incremental ones

params.name: once
params.help: Run a single cycle and exit with its status

params.name: max_runs
params.help: Stop after this many cycles, the first included

params.name: write_mode
params.help: How each cycle writes a table, as for `ingest`: overwrite or replace-runs

params.name: incremental_write
params.help: With --write-mode replace-runs, rewrite only the runs that changed instead of rebuilding the whole table.

params.name: drop_missing_runs
params.help: Remove the runs of a location added with `ingest --attach-run` that is not on this host. Without it, such a project stops the first cycle.

params.name: concurrency
params.help: Parallel HTTP requests during each cycle

params.name: dry_run
params.help: Report each cycle's changes without writing to the server

commands.name: nextflow
commands.help:
Print the path of the bundled Nextflow onComplete snippet.

Meant to be substituted straight into a Nextflow command, which is the whole
reason it exists: the snippet lives inside the installed package, and that is
not a path anyone should have to type or keep in sync.

    nextflow run nf-core/ampliseq --outdir results -c $(depictio config nextflow)

For an nf-core pipeline that is the entire setup. The snippet reads the
pipeline's own manifest and hands it to the CLI as --pipeline-id, which
resolves the bundled template, so there is nothing else to configure.

Use --print to read the snippet, or to copy it somewhere you can edit:

    depictio config nextflow --print > depictio.config

Use --install to stop repeating the -c, once per machine:

    depictio config nextflow --install

Every later `nextflow run` then triggers Depictio with no extra flag, and
`--uninstall` reverses it. Add --default-disabled to install it opt-in
instead: pipelines then need `--depictio_enabled true` to trigger. Either
way, `--depictio_enabled true/false` on a given `nextflow run` always wins.
commands.short_help: Print the path of the bundled Nextflow onComplete snippet.

params.name: print_
params.help: Write the snippet's contents to stdout instead of its path.

params.help: Undo --install, leaving any other Nextflow settings alone.

commands.name: push-images
commands.help:
Upload a directory of images to S3 storage, for an image data collection.
Formerly `images push`.

The directory structure is kept, relative to the source directory, and images
already in storage are skipped unless --overwrite. Upload to the collection's
s3_base_folder: its image_column paths are relative to it. `depictio ingest`
does this itself for a collection that sets local_images_path.

Examples:
    # Push all images to S3
    depictio data push-images ./data/images s3://my-bucket/project/images/

    # Dry run to see what would be uploaded
    depictio data push-images ./data/images s3://my-bucket/images/ --dry-run

    # Push only specific extensions
    depictio data push-images ./data/images s3://my-bucket/images/ --extensions ".png,.jpg"
commands.short_help: Upload a directory of images to S3 storage, for an image data collection. Formerly `images push`.

commands.name: vacuum
commands.help:
Remove Delta files no longer referenced by any retained version.

Nothing in depictio has ever vacuumed, so every re-ingestion has left its
predecessor's files behind and a data collection's physical footprint grows
without bound. A watcher accelerates that considerably.

Deliberately dry-run by default and never wired into an ingestion path:
vacuuming below the retention window pulls files out from under an API
worker that is part-way through reading the table.
commands.short_help: Remove Delta files no longer referenced by any retained version.

params.name: data_collection_tag
params.help: Data collection whose stale Delta files to remove

commands.name: validate
commands.help:
Validate a dashboard YAML file.

Runs two levels of validation:

1. Schema + domain (always): required fields, enum values, cross-field rules
   (visu_type, mode/code_content, aggregation×column_type, etc.)

2. Server schema (when a server is configured): resolves each component's
   workflow_tag + data_collection_tag against the server delta table schema, checks
   that column_name exists, and validates aggregation/interactive_component_type
   against the inferred column type. Without --server it uses the default server
   ($DEPICTIO_CLI_CONFIG_PATH, else ~/.depictio/CLI.yaml, else the local server),
   is skipped when that has no configuration, and what it reports is shown as
   warnings only. Use --offline to skip it.

Example:
    depictio dashboard validate dashboard.yaml --server local
    depictio dashboard validate dashboard.yaml --server admin_config.yaml --offline
    depictio dashboard validate dashboard.yaml  # offline unless a default server is set up

or ~/.depictio/CLI.yaml describes, else the local server (none needed for
--dry-run validation).

    depictio dashboard import dashboard.yaml --dry-run

    # Import into the server `depictio local up` runs
    depictio dashboard import dashboard.yaml --server local

    # Overwrite existing dashboard with same title
    depictio dashboard import dashboard.yaml --server admin_config.yaml --overwrite

    # Override with explicit project ID
    depictio dashboard import dashboard.yaml --server admin_config.yaml --project 646b0f3c1e4a2d7f8e5b8c9a

params.help: Refresh a project that exists: its configuration, and its tables with every run rescanned. Its runs become those of DATA_DIR (or of the project file's locations) and those added with --attach-run; the runs of any other location are removed. Its dashboards are kept as they are, edits made in the viewer included; the template's dashboards it lacks are added. A project not on the server yet is created.

params.name: attach_run
params.help: Add DATA_DIR to an EXISTING project as one more run, instead of creating a project. The run is recorded as attached, so a later --update-config keeps it. The project is found by --project, else by the template's own name. Implies --update-config, dashboards included. Only the new run's rows are written; a recipe that mixes samples (distances, ordinations, top-N) is recomputed over every run, see --per-run.

params.name: drop_missing_runs
params.help: On a refresh, remove the runs of a location added with --attach-run that is not on this host. Without it, such a refresh stops before changing anything.

params.help: Continue execution even if a step fails

params.help: When composing: also ingest the tabular files the catalog does not recognise, in an 'Other data' tab.

params.help: When composing: ingest the unrecognised files matching this glob, relative to DATA_DIR (e.g. 'stats/*.tsv'). Repeatable.

params.help: The pipeline that produced the data, as '<name>/<version>' (e.g. 'nf-core/ampliseq/2.16.0'). Without --template or --project-config-path, the bundled template that matches it is used; otherwise it is ignored. Pipeline triggers fill it in, from a Nextflow pipeline's workflow.manifest for instance.

params.name: triggered_by
params.help: What invoked this ingestion, recorded on the project and shown in its ingestion report. Defaults to 'manual'; a pipeline's completion trigger passes its engine (e.g. 'nextflow') so an automated project is distinguishable from one someone ingested by hand.

params.help: Provision (create-or-get) this user's account and run the pipeline as them, then emit a passwordless login link to their dashboard. Requires --provisioning-key.

params.name: provisioning_key
params.help: Shared provisioning secret used with --user (or set DEPICTIO_AUTH_PROVISIONING_API_KEY).

params.name: result_json
params.help: Write how the ingestion ended (status, project and dashboard ids and links) to this file as JSON, for scripts.

params.name: sync_changed
params.help: Re-upload only the files whose size or modification time moved since the last scan. Narrower than --update-config, which re-uploads every file.

params.name: write_mode
params.help: How step 6 writes a table. overwrite: rewrite it whole. replace-runs: partition it by run and rewrite only the runs in this batch, leaving the others untouched.

params.name: incremental_write
params.help: With --write-mode replace-runs, rewrite only the runs that changed instead of rebuilding the whole table. Falls back to a full rebuild whenever that cannot be done safely (run removed, table not partitioned by run, column type changed).

params.name: per_run
params.help: Compute every recipe once per run, including those that mix samples (distances, ordinations, top-N cuts), which are otherwise recomputed over all the project's runs at once. Their per-run outputs are then stacked.

params.name: skip_unchanged
params.help: Leave a data collection's table untouched when the scan found no new, changed or removed file for it. Off by default, so that ingesting again always rebuilds a project that drifted.

params.name: repartition
params.help: Let --write-mode replace-runs partition by run a table that is not yet. This rewrites every row, so it is never done implicitly, and never by the watcher.

params.name: streaming
params.help: Stream the Delta write instead of materialising the whole table in memory (lower peak RSS on large ingests). Experimental; falls back to the standard write on any failure.

commands.name: kinds
commands.help:
Emit the advanced_viz kind descriptors (source for tool-studio's kinds.json).

Shape: ``{"kinds": [ {viz_kind, label, description, icon, category,
required_roles, roles: {role: {required, dtypes, description}}, heavy} ]}``
— byte for byte what ``GET /advanced_viz/kinds`` returns, plus ``heavy``.

That equality is the point: Tool Studio has no backend, so its viz-kind
picker reads this snapshot where the app reads the endpoint. It used to
read a narrower map (roles flattened to a dtype list, a title-cased label,
no description or icon), which is why its picker could not be depictio's.
``heavy`` and ``role_names`` are the studio's two additions: those kinds
are computed by a Celery worker and cannot be previewed client-side at all,
and the role-name aliases let a backend-less picker rank kinds the way
``suggest_viz_kinds`` does server-side.
commands.short_help: Emit the advanced_viz kind descriptors (source for tool-studio's kinds.json).

params.name: as_json
params.help: Emit a machine-readable JSON map (for tool-studio).

params.name: output
params.help: Write the JSON here (default: stdout)

commands.name: manifest
commands.help:
Emit a JSON snapshot of the existing catalog (source for tool-studio's
catalog.json). Powers duplicate detection ("this tool already exists") and
"add a visualization to an existing tool" — so the web app can compare the
wizard against what is already in `depictio/catalog/` offline.

Per tool: identity + outputs; per output: id/slug/path_glob, declared
columns, existing `renders_as`, the repo-relative YAML path and its raw text
(so the app can append a render and open an update PR), and — when the
fixture is a small co-located CSV/TSV — its content, so new renders ground
and preview client-side exactly like an upload.
commands.short_help: Emit a JSON snapshot of the existing catalog (source for tool-studio's catalog.json). Powers duplicate detection ("this tool already exists") and "add a visualization to an existing tool" — so the web app can compare the wizard against what is already in `depictio/catalog/` offline.

params.name: as_json
params.help: Emit the machine-readable JSON (for tool-studio).

params.name: output
params.help: Write the JSON here (default: stdout)

commands.name: figure-params
commands.help:
Emit the figure builder's visualization list + per-viz parameter specs.

This is the exact payload the React figure builder fetches from
``/figure/visualizations`` and ``/figure/parameter-discovery/{viz_type}``.
Tool Studio seeds its builder store with this snapshot so depictio's real
figure UI renders offline (no backend). Shape::

    { "visualizations": [ {name, label, description, icon, group}, ... ],
      "params": { "<viz_type>": <VisualizationDefinition JSON>, ... } }

Derived from the pure Plotly-Express introspection in
``depictio/api/v1/services/figure/{definitions,parameter_discovery}.py`` —
the drift-free source the web app snapshots at build time.
commands.short_help: Emit the figure builder's visualization list + per-viz parameter specs.

params.name: as_json
params.help: Emit the machine-readable JSON (for tool-studio).

params.name: output
params.help: Write the JSON here (default: stdout)

commands.name: create
commands.help:
Create a new DC link for cross-DC filtering.

Examples:
    # Create a direct link between two table DCs
    depictio dev link create \
        --project-config-path project.yaml \
        --source-dc metadata_table \
        --source-column sample_id \
        --target-dc variants_table \
        --target-type table \
        --resolver direct

    # Create a sample_mapping link to a MultiQC DC
    depictio dev link create \
        --project-config-path project.yaml \
        --source-dc metadata_table \
        --source-column sample_id \
        --target-dc multiqc_general_stats \
        --target-type multiqc \
        --resolver sample_mapping
commands.short_help: Create a new DC link for cross-DC filtering.

commands.name: resolve
commands.help:
Test link resolution by resolving filter values from source to target DC.

This command tests the link resolution API by mapping source values
to target identifiers using the configured resolver.

    depictio dev link resolve \
        --project-config-path project.yaml \
        --source-dc metadata_table \
        --source-column sample_id \
        --target-dc multiqc_general_stats \
        --filter "S1,S2,S3"
